Subject: Post-call recap & next steps - encryption, retention, logging

Kevin / Aisha - thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of requirements we heard:
- Data classification: customer records will include PII (names, emails, masked payment references) and tokenized payment IDs.
- Retention: default retention for processed artifacts to be 90 days; some logs may need 1 year archival upon request.
- Logging/observability: audit logs, request/response traces, and token-level cost reporting needed for billing reconciliation.
- Data residency: production data must remain in US East region; EU-only workload for select customers is a future ask.
- Encryption: in-transit TLS required; at-rest AES-256 minimum. Customer asks about customer-managed keys (BYOK), HSM-backed keys, and envelope encryption.

Attachments: redwood-kms-options.pdf (summary of KMS/HSM support), soc2-audit-summary.pdf (latest SOC 2 scope). I’ve also included a one-pager on our data retention controls.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive to cover KMS options (BYOK vs Redwood-managed), key rotation, envelope encryption, and audit/export of key usage logs - propose 60m session.
2) Rishi from Security to join for the questions around key custody and SLA impact.
3) Draft mutual action plan (MAP) with timeline and required artifacts for procurement/security review.

Can you confirm the attendee list for the technical deep-dive and availability next week? I’ve CC’d Nikhil and Rishi to coordinate times.

Thanks Marissa - that summary is very helpful. A few clarifying questions before we schedule the deep-dive so we can pull the right folks from our side (security, infra):

1) Can Redwood support customer-managed keys for both hosted and dedicated deployments? If hosted, do keys ever leave the cloud KMS provider?
2) Do you support HSM-backed keys (like BYOK with customer HSM) or only cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault)?
3) Does envelope encryption apply to both model artifacts (weights/checkpoints) and inference logs/kv cache?
4) How granular are the audit logs for key usage and key access - can we export to our SIEM?
5) Any impact on SLA or latency for keys stored in a different region (we have EU customers on a separate tenant)?

Also: can you share a diagram (network/key flow) illustrating how a request is encrypted/decrypted when using customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed keys? That’ll help our security review.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Thanks Kevin - great questions. High-level answers below; we’ll cover details in the technical deep-dive and share architecture diagrams ahead of the session. I’ve attached a short comparison chart (kms-options-chart.xlsx).

1) Customer-managed keys (CMK/BYOK):
- Hosted API: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) in a Bring-Your-Own-Key model. Keys are never exported out of the KMS provider; Redwood holds ciphertext and only requests decryption operations from the KMS via secure RPCs.
- Dedicated/Private deployments: we support both customer KMS integrations and on-prem HSMs (PKCS#11-backed). For high-assurance needs, private deployments can be configured to use customer-owned HSMs where key material never leaves customer control.

2) HSM support:
- Yes - for Private deployments we support integration with customer HSMs (Thales, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM) and PKCS#11 interfaces. For Hosted, we rely on cloud KMS HSM protections provided by the cloud vendor.

3) Envelope encryption scope:
- Envelope encryption is applied to persisted artifacts (model checkpoints, persisted KV caches, logs at rest) by default. Live inference in RAM is transient and not persisted to disk; any persisted traces or logs are encrypted.

4) Audit logs & exports:
- Key usage is logged at the KMS provider level (e.g., CloudTrail for AWS) and we surface aggregated key-use metrics in the Redwood Console. We can configure real-time export of audit events to your SIEM (S3/Cloud Pub/Sub/Syslog endpoints) under the MAP.

5) Regional latency & SLA:
- If the KMS is in a different region there can be additional milliseconds of latency for remote decrypt calls. We recommend colocating KMS in the same region as the Redwood serving cluster for production workloads. SLA implications are handled per-deployment; dedicated contracts can include explicit availability guarantees and runbook for KMS failures (automatic fallback to Redwood-managed key with preapproved emergency process, if the customer opts in).

Next steps: Nikhil, can you propose 2x 60-minute slots (this week) for the technical deep-dive? Rishi - can you confirm what artifacts PayWise will need for SOC/cryptographic review?

Links: architecture diagram (https://drive.redwood.com/arch/kms-arch-diagram.pdf) - I’ll upload a version with callouts ahead of the session.

Thanks,
